subject.title: feat(mcp): stage binary tool content for relay

question: Should OpenClaw core own automatic staging and relay of MCP binary tool-result content through the existing `details.media` path, using a bounded process-local host-owned-path registry?
rationale: The implementation is intentionally channel-agnostic and preserves the existing external-tool filter for arbitrary paths, but it adds a new user-visible relay behavior and a trust exception that cannot be selected from source correctness alone.

options.title: Accept the generic relay foundation
options.body: Keep the bounded host-owned staging path in core, require current-head channel proof, and leave channel-specific presentation and broader MCP contracts to follow-up work.

options.title: Require a public attachment contract first
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers define a plugin or SDK-level attachment and transcript contract rather than extending the internal relay-details seam.

options.title: Limit the initial rollout
options.body: Land only a narrower documented channel or MCP surface after maintainers select the supported transport and upgrade scope.

recommendation.title: Accept the generic relay foundation
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded host-owned staging path in core, require current-head channel proof, and leave channel-specific presentation and broader MCP contracts to follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on MCP result coercion makes this person the closest available history-based routing candidate for the materialization boundary.
